# When Will AGI Arrive? Expert Timelines and Predictions

Quick answer

No one knows, and serious forecasts differ by decades. As of September 2026, the heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind expect AGI or comparably powerful AI between late 2026 and about 2030, the Metaculus forecasting community's median is 2031, and the latest edition of the largest recurring survey of AI researchers puts a 50 percent chance on 2042. Much of that spread comes from forecasters predicting different things under the same word.

SS

Shailey Singh

Editor-in-Chief, Santage · Research: Santage Research · Editorial standards

Published: September 24, 2026 Last Updated: September 24, 2026 Reviewed: Shailey Singh, Editor-in-Chief

"When will AGI arrive?" is among the most asked questions in artificial intelligence, and in 2026 it stopped being hypothetical. OpenAI's chief executive now says his company will have a system he would call AGI before the end of this year. The median AI researcher, asked the same question in a formal survey, says 2042. Both answers are sincere, both are on the record, and they are sixteen years apart.

This pillar collects every serious AGI forecast in one place, each one attributed to a named person or organization with a date and a link to the primary record. It explains why the forecasts disagree, what the hard evidence on AI progress actually shows, which past predictions have already been tested, and what would move the date earlier or later. Forecasts are labeled as forecasts. The page is reviewed monthly, because this is the fastest moving question in the field.

Key takeaways

- Lab leaders say this decade: Sam Altman expects an internal system he would call AGI by the end of 2026 (TIME, August 2026). Dario Amodei guesses one to three years for "powerful AI" (February 2026). Demis Hassabis broadly expects AGI around 2030 (May 2026).
- Forecasters say early 2030s: The Metaculus community median for a general AI system is April 2031, with a central range from 2028 to 2037, as of September 24, 2026.
- Researchers say 2040s: 1,580 AI researchers surveyed in December 2024 put a 50 percent chance of high-level machine intelligence at 2042, five years earlier than the 2023 survey and nearly two decades earlier than the 2016 survey.
- Expert panels are slower still: The Forecasting Research Institute's expert panel gives a median of 2050 and its superforecasters 2047, for AGI that beats top professionals on nearly all non-physical work.
- The evidence is moving fast: The length of software tasks AI agents can complete has doubled about every 4.3 months since 2023, and METR measured an early Claude Mythos Preview at a 50 percent time horizon of at least 16 hours in March 2026.
- The declaration has started, informally: When OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on September 3, 2026, its president Greg Brockman said "it's not unreasonable to feel that we are now in the AGI era." OpenAI has not formally declared AGI, and independent experts disagree.
- Definitions drive the gap: Altman's 2026 claim uses OpenAI's economic definition. Stricter definitions that require continual learning and reliability, including Santage's, are not met by any system as of September 2026.
- The Santage read: AGI declarations are arriving before any independent verification. Track the definition, the evidence, and the verifier, not just the year.

## When will AGI arrive? The short answer

There is no consensus date for artificial general intelligence, and anyone who gives a single year with confidence is ahead of the evidence. What exists is a spread of dated, attributable forecasts that cluster into three bands as of September 2026.

1. 2026 to 2030: the leaders of the frontier labs, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and xAI, plus prediction markets and the most aggressive independent forecasters.
2. Early to mid 2030s: the Metaculus forecasting community, independent modelers such as some AI Futures Project authors, and prominent researchers who expect current methods to need one or two more breakthroughs.
3. 2040s and later: large surveys of AI researchers, panels of experts and superforecasters, and skeptics who argue that today's methods will not get there on their own or that economic transformation takes decades.

These bands are not measuring the same event. AGI is a contested term, and the earliest forecasts tend to use the narrowest definitions. Santage's working definition, used across all our AGI coverage, is demanding: an AI system that can match or exceed capable human performance across the broad range of cognitive tasks a person can do, including learning new skills it was not trained for, transferring knowledge across domains, and reasoning reliably. For the full case behind that definition, see What Is AGI?

As of September 24, 2026, no AI system meets a rigorous definition of AGI. Lab leaders forecast AGI or comparably powerful AI between late 2026 and about 2030, forecasting platforms center on the early 2030s, and surveys of AI researchers center on the 2040s.

## What do the AI lab leaders predict?

The people running the largest AI labs give the shortest timelines, and in 2026 several of them sharpened their dates.

### OpenAI: AGI by the end of 2026

In an interview published by TIME on August 26, 2026, Sam Altman said OpenAI was "not quite yet" at AGI but would have an internal system he would call AGI by the end of 2026. He was using the definition in the OpenAI Charter: "highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work." The claim centered on Astra, a family of models OpenAI was then previewing to customers. Altman described it as the first model where "the model actually invents new things in a way that matters."

One week later, on September 3, 2026, OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 Astra, four weeks after it had paused the model over critical cybersecurity risk. At launch, OpenAI president Greg Brockman told Fortune: "It's not unreasonable to feel that we are now in the AGI era, and I think that if you want to say this [model is] the first one, I think it's reasonable." That is the closest any frontier lab has come to claiming AGI. It is not a formal declaration: OpenAI has not said Astra meets its charter definition, and independent researchers quoted by Information Age, along with the ARC Prize Foundation, disputed the framing.

OpenAI has also published intermediate goals that can be checked. In October 2025 Altman wrote that the company had set internal goals of an automated AI research intern by September 2026 and a true automated AI researcher by March 2028. On September 6, 2026, OpenAI said (Santage coverage) it now has a system that can carry out well-defined research tasks under human direction, including tasks that would take a skilled researcher a few days, while noting that its agents "still require significant human steering." That assessment is OpenAI's own and has not been independently evaluated.

"We have set internal goals of having an automated AI research intern by September of 2026 running on hundreds of thousands of GPUs, and a true automated AI researcher by March of 2028. We may totally fail at this goal..."

Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, October 29, 2025. Read the source

### Anthropic: "powerful AI" in late 2026 or early 2027

Anthropic's CEO avoids the term AGI and describes "powerful AI," a system with capabilities "matching or exceeding that of Nobel Prize winners across most disciplines," able to work autonomously for hours to weeks. In a March 2025 submission to the White House, Anthropic said it expected such systems "will emerge in late 2026 or early 2027."
